newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi says Publitalia accounts clean.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi says Publitalia accounts clean.

text.p: Italian media mogul Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday the accounts of his Publitalia advertising group were completely clean.

"The magistrates' inquiries have shown that Publitalia does not have a separate accounting system, it does not have slush funds and no false invoices," he told reporters after appearing as a defence witness in the trial of former Publitalia chairman Marcello Dell'Utri in the north-western city of Turin.
Dell'Utri is charged with false billing and tax fraud and has denied wrongdoing. Publitalia is part of Berlusconi's Mediaset group.
Berlusconi said he had tried to show during his testimony that Publitalia was completely outside any allegations of wrong-doing. The court case, which began in June, was continuing.
Berlusconi is on trial in a separate case on corruption charges related to his Fininvest business empire.

The prosecution alleges that Publitalia and two of its subsidiaries Publieuropa and Publiespana created some nine billion lire of assets through inflated bills for sporting sponsorships which were not recorded in company books.
The cash was allegedly spent in various ways, including hand-outs to business associates.

Dell'Utri's lawyer Oreste Dominioni has said the only person responsible for the affair was Gianpaolo Prandelli, former Publitalia deputy general manager, who has accepted a reduced 18-month prison sentence under a plea-bargaining deal before the trial began.
